ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the 2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) to assess state-specific prevalence estimates
Prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals for cigarette smoking, smokeless tobacco use
Current cigarette smoking ranged from 9.7% (Utah) to 26.7% (West Virginia)
Cigarette smoking was significantly higher among males than females in 34 states
The prevalence of any cigarette and/or smokeless tobacco use differed significantly by race/ethnicity in 21 states
The BRFSS is an annual state-based telephone (landline and cell phone) survey
CDC analyzed data from the 2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)

methods_quotes.q: were calculated overall and by state and sex
Because of limited sample size, data were stratified by race/ethnicity for current any cigarette and/or smokeless tobacco use
Data were weighted to adjust for nonresponse and to yield state representative estimates.
Chi-square tests were conducted to assess differences among groups, with p<0.05 considered to be statistically significant.
Chi-square test assessed for differences between males and females; significant level p<0.05.
Chi-square test assessed for differences within the four race/ethnicity categories; significant level p<0.05.
